messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I don’t know what the will says, and I’m not agreeing to a discounted purchase. Get an independent valuation and share the will with all three of us before we discuss price or process. I want a fair share, but there’s no need to rush.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband, at a family discount, but I don’t have a price or terms settled. I know C hasn’t agreed. I’m not sure what the will says.
Thank you. The house matters to me, but I’m not sure what should happen with it yet. And yes, item 2 reflects my view; some money toward starting a dance studio would mean a lot.
Yes, I agree we should share the will and get an independent valuation first. I don’t know who the executor is or who has the will.
Yes, sharing the will and getting an independent valuation sound like sensible first steps. I’m afraid I don’t know who the executor is or who has the will.
I don’t know who the executor is or where the will is. Let’s check Dad’s papers and contact his lawyer.
I can help look through Dad’s papers. I don’t know his lawyer’s name.
Yes, checking Dad’s papers and contacting his lawyer seem sensible. I don’t know the lawyer’s name, I’m afraid.
Yes. I’ll go through Dad’s papers with A.
Sure, C—when works for you? I’ll share anything we find with B.
That sounds sensible, thank you. I’ll wait to see the will and valuation before considering what should happen with the house.
